title: Motion Graphs
summary: Builds a directed graph of captured clips and synthesized transitions; graph walks satisfy user constraints such as locomotion paths.
limitations: Coverage depends on captured motions and viable graph connections; no open-vocabulary semantic generation.

title: Interactive Motion Generation from Examples
summary: Cuts and pastes mocap via randomized hierarchical graph search under constraints at interactive speeds.
limitations: Reuses available examples; source coverage bounds the realizable actions.

title: Motion Synthesis from Annotations
summary: Uses annotated action timelines and multiscale dynamic programming to assemble motion, including overlapping qualitative constraints.
limitations: Requires an annotated motion database; a timeline label does not provide unseen interaction geometry.
method: Coarse-to-fine dynamic programming searches database motion blocks; SVM-assisted annotation expands a small labeled subset.
conditions: Positive, negative and unconstrained timeline labels; optional pose, position and orientation constraints.
evaluation: Interactive examples include trip, run and jump constraints and combined walking/carrying semantics.

title: Parametric Motion Graphs
summary: Connects parameterized motion synthesis with valid dynamically generated blending transitions.
limitations: Example-based blend spaces require appropriate source coverage and valid transitions.

title: TEACH: Temporal Action Composition for 3D Humans
summary: Generates ordered action sequences using a hierarchical Transformer: parallel within each action and autoregressive between actions.
limitations: Uses sequential BABEL supervision; autoregressive rollout and transition continuity require separate assessment.
method: Hierarchical action-level autoregression with non-autoregressive motion generation inside each action.
conditions: Ordered natural-language descriptions and action lengths; prior generated action context.
evaluation: BABEL sequential text-motion compositions and multiple baselines; no object-conditioned manipulation benchmark claimed.
code_note: Former author username athnnik is stale; current author repository verified 2026-11-19.

title: SINC: Spatial Composition of 3D Human Motions for Simultaneous Action Generation
summary: Uses language-model action-to-body-part assignments to stitch motions and augment training for simultaneous-action generation.
limitations: Compatible part assignments do not guarantee physical feasibility or coherent object contact.
method: GPT-3 identifies active body parts; body-part motion combinations create synthetic examples for text-to-motion training.
conditions: Text specifying simultaneous actions and a body-part inventory.
evaluation: Compositional generation compared with baselines; improvement from synthetic part compositions is reported.

title: Human Motion Diffusion as a Generative Prior
summary: Introduces DoubleTake sequential composition, ComMDM two-person coordination and DiffusionBlending joint-control model composition.
limitations: DoubleTake needs overlap and refinement design; ComMDM needs interaction examples; composition is not guaranteed physical validity.
method: A frozen short-motion diffusion prior is reused for overlapping prompted intervals; a second take refines transitions. Separate small adapters or fine-tuned controlled priors support other composition modes.
conditions: Interval text prompts; two-person motion examples for ComMDM; prescribed joint or trajectory motion for fine-grained control.
evaluation: Off-the-shelf motion diffusion prior compared with task-specific trained models across sequential, parallel and controlled-generation tasks.

title: DiffCollage: Parallel Generation of Large Content with Diffusion Models
summary: Factor-graph composition aggregates diffusion outputs over overlapping pieces for large parallel generation, including long text-guided motion.
limitations: Generic overlap approximation; motion-specific contact and global semantic correctness are not guaranteed.

title: MultiAct: Long-Term 3D Human Motion Generation from Multiple Action Labels
summary: Recurrently conditions on prior motion and the next action label to generate transitions and long multi-action sequences.
limitations: Action-label conditioning is less expressive than free text; recurrent rollout requires long-horizon drift checks.
year_basis: First public preprint in December 2022; revised 2023.

title: Sequential Texts Driven Cohesive Motions Synthesis with Natural Transitions
summary: Combines previous/current text semantics with learnable transition tokens and a transition loss.
limitations: Representation and evaluation protocol differ from some BABEL baselines; direct score comparisons need matching representations.

title: AMD: Autoregressive Motion Diffusion
summary: Introduces HumanLong3D and conditions iterative diffusion generation on current text plus previous text and action sequences.
limitations: Long-text paired data construction and autoregressive accumulated error deserve inspection.

title: AMD: Anatomical Motion Diffusion with Interpretable Motion Decomposition and Fusion
summary: Parses complex text into anatomical scripts and fuses script and text guidance in diffusion.
limitations: Depends on language-model decomposition quality; do not conflate with the unrelated Autoregressive Motion Diffusion AMD.

title: Seamless Human Motion Composition with Blended Positional Encodings
summary: FlowMDM mixes absolute and relative positional encodings to jointly generate seamless sequences from changing interval prompts.
limitations: Single-human kinematic synthesis; finite attention horizon and text timing remain design constraints, with no object-contact certification.
method: Early denoising uses absolute positions for within-action structure; late denoising uses relative positions across boundaries. Pose-centric cross-attention associates each frame with its own condition.
conditions: Non-overlapping text intervals and durations; can train on singly described clips.
evaluation: BABEL and HumanML3D subsequence and transition quality, plus Peak Jerk and Area Under Jerk for discontinuities.

title: Multi-Track Timeline Control for Text-Driven 3D Human Motion Generation
summary: STMC combines text intervals that can overlap, assigning body-part tracks and stitching explicit pose predictions at each denoising step.
limitations: Prompt-to-part assignment and incompatible overlaps require care; kinematic composition does not establish interaction physics.
method: Preprocesses prompts into per-body-part timelines; denoises local crops and combines corresponding pose components repeatedly during sampling.
conditions: Multi-track text timeline with timing and body-part assignments, provided by user or language model.
evaluation: Temporal and simultaneous composition; assess under the paper’s timeline setting rather than single-prompt metrics alone.

title: T2LM: Long-Term 3D Human Motion Generation from Multiple Sentences
summary: Uses a local 1D-convolutional VQ-VAE decoder to decode a continuous text-predicted latent stream, trained on short clips.
limitations: Local receptive fields favor smooth joins but do not guarantee global scene/contact consistency.

title: DART: A Diffusion-Based Autoregressive Motion Model for Real-Time Text-Driven Motion Control
summary: Latent diffusion predicts motion primitives from history and current text; noise optimization or RL provides spatial control.
limitations: Autoregressive primitive history is local; spatial control and scene tasks should be evaluated separately.

title: MotionCLIP: Exposing Human Motion Generation to CLIP Space
summary: Aligns a motion autoencoder with CLIP text and rendered-image embeddings to support semantic edits and interpolation.
limitations: Semantic latent arithmetic offers no strict preservation or physical-contact guarantee.

title: MotionFix: Text-Driven 3D Human Motion Editing
summary: Collects source/target/edit-text triplets and trains TMED conditional diffusion; proposes retrieval-based editing evaluation.
limitations: Editing quality must jointly measure requested change and source preservation; retrieval metrics alone do not certify both.

title: Pay Attention and Move Better: Harnessing Attention for Interactive Motion Generation and Training-free Editing
summary: MotionCLR explicitly models word-motion correspondence and manipulates attention for interactive generation edits.
limitations: Training-free editing refers to inference operations on a trained model, not absence of model training.
title_note: First preprint title: MotionCLR: Motion Generation and Training-free Editing via Understanding Attention Mechanisms.

title: MotionLab: Unified Human Motion Generation and Editing via the Motion-Condition-Motion Paradigm
summary: Unifies generation and editing tasks through a motion-condition-motion formulation, including text, trajectory, style and in-between tasks.
limitations: Unified task coverage does not imply every task has equal supervision or generalization; inspect per-task protocol.

title: MoMask: Generative Masked Modeling of 3D Human Motions
summary: Residual-quantized motion tokens and masked modeling provide high-quality text-conditioned generation and flexible completion.
limitations: Discrete framewise tokens constrain joint-level editing granularity; baseline generation is not a full composition benchmark.

title: MMM: Generative Masked Motion Model
summary: Text-conditioned masked motion tokens support in-betweening, body-part changes and long sequence synthesis.
limitations: Mask-defined edits require a clear preserved region; token reconstruction and motion preservation should be checked.

title: BAMM: Bidirectional Autoregressive Motion Model
summary: Bidirectional autoregressive motion-token generation predicts ending and supports completion and long-sequence synthesis.
limitations: Long composition is an additional application; detailed semantics and transition protocol require separate checks.

title: ParCo: Part-Coordinating Text-to-Motion Synthesis
summary: Separate part tokenizers and lightweight generators communicate through a coordination module.
limitations: Part-factorized architecture is not itself evidence of arbitrary simultaneous action composition.

title: Motion Mamba: Efficient and Long Sequence Motion Generation
summary: Hierarchical temporal and bidirectional spatial state-space blocks improve long-motion modeling and efficiency.
limitations: Long single-prompt generation differs from ordered multi-prompt composition.

title: MixerMDM: Learnable Composition of Human Motion Diffusion Models
summary: Learns adversarial dynamic mixing of pretrained single-person and interaction diffusion models.
limitations: Requires learning a mixer; model composition differs from constructing a reusable motion dataset.

title: FrankenMotion: Part-level Human Motion Generation and Composition
summary: Uses asynchronous atomic part-level text annotations and part-aware diffusion for spatial and temporal control.
limitations: LLM-generated part annotations and adapted benchmark baselines need auditing; abstract promises release rather than proving current reproducibility.

title: Towards Decompositional Human Motion Generation with Energy-Based Diffusion Models
summary: DeMoGen learns reusable motion concepts through composed energy distributions using explicit, orthogonal self-supervised or semantic-consistency training.
limitations: No individual-concept motion ground truth is required, but semantic disentanglement remains an empirical claim; repository release checklist is incomplete.

title: PRISM: Streaming Human Motion Generation with Per-Joint Latent Decomposition
summary: Kinematic-unit continuous latents, causal VAE and flow matching support prefix continuation, segment chaining and narrative composition.
limitations: Large-model and dataset-scale effects must be separated from factorization; no interaction physics guarantee.
publication_note: Abstract-level record only. A later HTML revision appears under a different title; version alignment needs further review before method-level claims.

title: CoMA: Compositional Human Motion Generation with Multi-modal Agents
summary: Collaborating language/vision agents control a part-specific masked motion generator and self-correction for detailed long prompts and editing.
limitations: Agent decomposition and visual self-critique add dependencies; user studies on rich prompts are distinct from benchmark distribution metrics.
year_basis: First public preprint 2024; later venue not independently checked in this intake.

title: Streaming Multi-Track Timeline Control for 3D Human Motion Generation
summary: TimelineControl combines interval-aware conditioning, causal part representations and part-aware denoising with TimelineMotion annotations.
limitations: New preprint; comparative claims apply to evaluated streaming baselines and require independent replication.
